FoE undertake a lot of legal action against the UK Government
They lobby for their demands to be met within UK legislation

Their latest campaign is the Big Climate Plan, which began in 2025
Additional Info: Their work aligns with the worker-climate movement but they aren’t working in direct collaboration with unions or workers. They mainly focus on taking legal action for UK legislation, which if successful, has a positive impact on the worker-climate movement.

Group Intro: Friends of the Earth Scotland is a Scottish environmental campaigning organisation working on climate justice, fossil fuel phaseout and a fair transition to a zero-carbon economy. In the worker-climate movement, its most relevant work focuses on green jobs, oil and gas transition, public ownership of energy and putting workers and communities at the centre of transition planning.
Key Group Activities: Campaigning for public investment in green jobs, infrastructure, training, public services and a just recovery, including through its Green Jobs Recovery plan.
Working with oil and gas workers, trade unions and communities to develop worker-led just transition demands, including through the Our Power project and its wider Just Transition campaign.

Producing research and campaigning for a managed phaseout of oil and gas, no new extraction, renewable-energy expansion and protection for affected workers and regions, including through SeaChange and No New Oil & Gas.

Supporting workers facing an unjust transition, including expressing solidarity with Grangemouth refinery workers and calling for investment in a transition plan with workers and trade unions at its centre.
Additional Info: FoES is not a trade union, but works across the climate and labour movements through worker engagement, policy research and collaboration with trade unions, community organisations and groups including Platform, Oil Change International and the Just Transition Partnership.

Their aim is to “build a new economy” which “puts people and the planet first”. Their work focuses on issues relating to the climate, housing, migration and far-right politics.

Group Intro: The original Lucas Plan was a movement of arms manufacturing workers in the 1970s to defend their jobs by proposing a more socially useful service of their skills and technology. The New Lucas Plan was established at the 40th anniversary conference of the Lucas Plan in 2016 as discussions led to plans around the idea of a ‘just transition’ and what that means for local communities, union action and industry.
Key Group Activities: Provides a network for environmentally and socially conscious trade unions and grassroots organisations.
Pursues a whole-of-society approach, calling for a new economic model that meets social needs within environmental limits.
Their work focuses on 4 core areas: arms conversion, robotics and automation, just transition and democratic local planning.
They organise events such as webinars to share ideas and build cross-movement networks.
Additional Info: The New Lucas Plan clearly stipulates 9 principles that are required to fulfil a just transition. Although they recognise that a just transition is needed as a response to climate change, their principles to achieve it are grounded in human rights and social protection, with an emphasis on unionised jobs and collective bargaining.

Key Group Activities: Coordinate and promote the role of Green Representatives
Work to mainstream climate action and adaptation across the union and society as a whole
Lobby for a National Climate Service
Engage with and support climate action campaigns across the wider climate movement
Set up a National Climate Service Working Group in April 2022, which commissioned the Public Services International Research Unit (PSIRU) in March 2023
Additional Info: PCS Green Workplaces call for a unionised whole-of-society approach in responding to climate change, demanding public ownership and the creation of a National Climate Service. They are involved in many campaigns that go beyond the scope of the trade union itself. The resources they use are often taken from TUC Green Workplaces, meaning they are coherent and coordinated with the wider worker-climate movement. PCS’s declaration of a climate emergency in 2019 sent a strong message that the Green Workplaces group/campaign would be mainstreamed across the union.

Group Intro: TUCAN is a cross-union network campaigning for air pollution, particularly occupational and indoor air pollution, to be recognised and acted on as a workplace health and safety issue. It is hosted by the Greener Jobs Alliance.
Key Group Activities: Producing practical guidance and campaign resources and a Clean Air Charter to help workers, union reps and health and safety reps identify and act on workplace air pollution.
Supporting workplace air quality monitoring and evidence gathering in a range of sectors.

Intervening in policy and regulatory processes to push for occupational and indoor air pollution to be recognised in clean air policy, with stronger standards, enforcement, workplace risk assessments and worker/union consultation.

Organising seminars, events and cross-movement activity that bring together trade unionists, campaigners, academics, public health actors and local/regional authorities around air pollution and climate risks.
Additional Info: TUCAN appears to be a cross-union network rather than a formal structure of one union.
It is closely linked to the trade union movement through supporting unions, TUC/TUC regional activity, trades councils, union officers, health and safety reps and green reps.
It also works closely with the Greener Jobs Alliance and Hazards Campaign, alongside groups such as the Healthy Air Coalition, local authorities, academic researchers and air quality specialists.

Group Intro: Workers Co-op is a co-operative which was set up in October 2022. The group is made up of more than 55 worker co-op organisations and workers with an annual turnover of £100,000. It has a Board of Directors, but day-to-day management and delivery is sociocratically run by its 35 workers members. Their Own The Future campaign sees democratic worker ownership as key to building caring, ecological and abundant local economies. The campaign is loosely relevant to the worker-climate movement as it supports the establishment of new worker co-ops in pursuit of a worker-led transition.
Key Group Activities: Own The Future campaign - a one year co-op support programme, which started in March 2026, which provides mentoring, training and financial support for 5 selected new worker co-ops.
Hosting events such as organising weekends away with full schedules of workshops and networking talks
Sharing resources and best practices on their website
Additional Info: Their work is loosely related to the worker-climate movement, but not explicitly. Their Own The Future campaign frames worker co-ops as the way to achieve a successful social and ecological transition, but their focus remains on providing support for workers involved or interested in forming a co-op. The group doesn’t demonstrate any environmental/climate change awareness past their view that worker co-ops are necessary for a sustainable economic future.

The environment is mentioned briefly in the Worker Co-op’s Code, but only in terms of trying to avoid producing harm to local communities, rather than in acknowledgement of the wider context of climate change and climate action.

GKN Solidarity Campaign Info: In July 2021, the announced closure of the GKN Driveline factory in Florence led the workers to establish the GKN Factory Collective and take over the factory, with a plan to establish a social cooperative to produce cargo bikes and solar panels.
Climate Justice Coalition allied with the Collective and helped to raise awareness and fundraise for the campaign by organising events and facilitating the international solidarity movement.

CJC helped to convene a delegation of trade unionists from the UK to participate in assemblies and protests around the GKN factory in Florence. The delegation included representatives from the RMT, FBU, IWGB, UCU, Safe Landing, Greener Jobs Alliance, and others.

CJC launched a fundraising campaign to purchase shares in the Workers’ Collective. This campaign was successful, with CJC becoming shareholders in the new workers co-op in October 2024, and continued to expand, with 1,800 participating entities and raising over 1 million euros by July 2026.

Group Name: Equity for a Green New Deal
Group Intro: Equity for a Green New Deal is a network of Equity members organising for climate justice in the performing arts and entertainment industries. The network campaigns around sustainable and accessible workplaces, greening Equity’s own operations, fossil fuel divestment and solidarity with workers fighting for a green and just future.
Key Group Activities: Pension divestment and green finance: Equity for a Green New Deal campaigned for the Equity Pension Scheme to cut ties with fossil fuels, beginning with a 2017 campaign around the pension fund’s fossil fuel exposure. Equity later moved the whole default Equity Pension fund, worth over £130m, into a greener fund with extensive fossil fuel exclusions, and members also called on the Chancellor to unlock green investment through pension reform.

Green Rider campaign: The group created the Green Rider campaign, including the Green Rider Handshake, a template actors can use at the job-offer stage to raise sustainability demands with productions. Related resources include the Equity Green Rider template and Ten Sustainability Commitments for TV & Film, which cover travel, accommodation, energy use, materials, waste, catering, environmental audits, green skills and training, and reducing emissions across production. The Green Rider has been piloted on BBC and Sky Studios productions and is being negotiated into Equity’s collective agreements with PACT (the producers’ industry body).

Sustainable theatre/Theatre Green Book work: Equity for a Green New Deal established a sustainable theatre working group and engaged with the Theatre Green Book. Its feedback pushes for stronger worker and union voice in theatre sustainability standards, alongside accessibility, greater ambition, fossil fuel divestment, sustainable investment principles and more practical routes for implementation.

Heat safety and climate-related working conditions: Equity for a Green New Deal is linked to Equity’s Too Hot to Work organising around unsafe workplace heat during heatwaves. The heatwave briefing was aimed at Equity deputies and activists across live performance and recorded media, helping members stay safe, organise colleagues to demand heat mitigation measures and plan action during the Heat Strike week with wider TUC, Heat Strike and Hazards activity.
Additional Info: Equity for a Green New Deal appears to be an official Equity member network rather than an external campaign group. Equity’s network page says members can join the Green New Deal Network and that it meets once a month on Zoom.

The group’s work combines internal union change, industry-facing campaigns, bargaining-related resources, policy demands and cross-movement collaboration. It has worked or interacted with PACT through the Green Rider collective agreement work, the Theatres Trust through the Theatre Green Book process, and wider climate/worker campaigns through Heat Strike, Hazards, the TUC and fossil fuel phaseout campaigning.

The network also supports a managed phaseout of oil and gas production, large-scale clean job creation, funded retraining and protection of workers’ rights. Equity’s signing of the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty also appears linked to the network’s wider role in mainstreaming climate issues into Equity’s union work and industrial agreements.

Group Name: Green UNISON (also known as the Year of Green Activity campaign)
Group Intro: According to a UNISON article taken from their website, Green UNISON is an ongoing campaign which was set up in September 2020 and is used as an umbrella term for all UNISON’s green activities. But according to another of their articles (a report of a members survey) Green UNISON is a union network of green activists who have been internally lobbying for green policies within UNISON since 2017.

Their aims/demands include achieving net zero emissions and a just transition in public services, and their tactics include raising awareness, increasing the number of branch environmental officers, using union structures for engagement on climate change, and showcasing environmental work on branch agendas. The demands of this group were mainstreamed into the union when UNISON passed its green motion in 2022.
Key Group Activities: Internal lobbying for UNISON to adopt a green motion (which was successful in 2022) and to encourage further climate action across the union
Produce a newsletter which includes information on training opportunities and events
Host events to build the Green UNISON network and raise awareness of climate change and environmental issues within the union
Support the UNISON members surveys on climate change and a just transition
Collaborate with research institutions to produce reports and policy recommendations for how to decarbonise the public sector
Create resources such as a model motion to encourage branches to strengthen the role of green reps and engage with UNISON Green Week activities
Facilitate green rep training and networking sessions
Additional Info: The Green UNISON group began as a grassroots movement within the union by local environmental officers and branch reps. Its name is now used synonymously with UNISON’s Year of Green Activity 2026 campaign, which suggests the original movement was successful at campaigning for more green activity within UNISON.
Though it can’t be clearly attributed to the internal lobbying of Green UNISON, UNISON became the first UK union to sign the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty in 2024.
There are no publications by Green UNISON specifically, due to the group’s work being officially absorbed into mainstream UNISON activities.

Group Intro: Just Transition Wakefield was created in 2019 by Wakefield and District Trades Council in partnership with Wakefield Friends of the Earth, as an alliance between local grass roots and community organisations. Support for the Wakefield Good Food partnership in conjunction with other local groups across Wakefield.

Group Intro: Trade Unions for Energy Democracy (TUED) was formed as a result of a Global Trade Union Roundtable in 2012, which was organised by the Global Labour Institute
TUED is an international network of unions calling for public ownership of energy as a means to achieve a just transition

TUED is critical of existing international environmental and economic governance structures, as these institutions favour profits and neoliberalism over public goods and workers’ rights, or as they call it, “social power”
They argue that public ownership of energy would both support efforts to protect the climate and improve democratic accountability

TUED brings together unions from around the world to help create a coherent and coordinated trade union demand for a just transition that is centred around workers and which will require a full socioeconomic transformation to achieve
Key Group Activities: Produce regular research reports to disseminate knowledge and help support a unified cross-union understanding of a just transition
Bi-monthly global forums to build international union networks and strengthen common understanding of just transition demands
TUED South Platform was launched to specifically support Global South unions
Their Trade Union Task Force helped to develop the Trade Union Program for a Public Low-Carbon Energy Future, which was launched at COP26 in 2021
They produce a regular e-bulletin
They ask affiliated unions to provide funds to the group which helps them support a wide range of campaigns
Additional Info: TUED is very international in scope and their demands are very broad and are not specific to national contexts or sectors
When they discuss public ownership, they are generally referring to energy in particular
Most of their reports/working papers are produced in collaboration with Cornell University and the Rosa Luxemburg Stiftung NYC
Sean Sweeney from the City University of New York is the main TUED report author
They are financed by their affiliated unions
They have been linked to many case studies that take a conference format

Group Name: UCU Green Reps (and Climate and Ecological Emergency Committee (CEEC))
Group Intro: The role of UCU Green Reps was established in 2008 alongside the launch of the TUC's Green Workplaces project. The group functions as an official branch of UCU and, as of May 2025, is in the process of forming regular network forums for its reps to share experiences and coordinate their work. In 2022, the UCU National Executive Committee established the Climate and Ecological Emergency Committee (CEEC) to spearhead the UCU's Green New Deal and Just Transition Framework initiatives. The CEEC has also taken on the role of coordinating the Green Reps network to create a unified internal lobbying effort, seeking to embed environmental demands into UCU as a whole.
Key Group Activities: Participate in green bargaining within their branches to pursue the demand for UCU's Green New Deal and Just Transition Framework
The CEEC produces a quarterly Green Futures Newsletter
The CEEC organises annual meetings where motions are drafted to be proposed at the UCU Congresses
Green Reps raise awareness of green issues and promote the signing of a formalised workplace agreement on 'greening the workplace'
Green Reps often negotiate in collaboration with student groups/unions within universities
Additional Info: The group operates as an official UCU structure, with the union developing resources for the green reps to use
UCU conducted a survey of its green reps to learn how to best support them in their work

Group Intro: The WCCA is an international organisation that brings a focus on working class communities in regards to the green transition. They both champaign the social classes ideologies and risks in regards to climate change, somewhat based in a Marxian tradition of class and change.
Key Group Activities: Advocacy - public talks, panel discussions, podcast appearances etc.
Workshops - so far only 5 workshops have been conducted, but they have largely focused on movement building
Resource creation - made a communications toolkit
Heat strike - work with a UK based campaign with various unions to bring a maximum working temperature law and a heat related furlough scheme
Policy consultation - providing advice to a range of actors about best practise in regards to social inclusion and climate action
Additional Info: They have only been in operation for a few years (started in 2023) and the speed in which they built movement capacity and institutional recognition is incredible. Made up of individuals who have experience in a range of fields from political activism to climate science, the holistic voice that they provide is crucial to the wider movement. They have a notable connection to Unison, helping launch their campaign “Workers and Community United: Environmental Action From Below” in Yorkshire and the broader North East of England. While they seem to have a UK focus, on the basis that the group started in the UK and have the largest membership group there, they do also have significant outreach internationally and are working to expand it.
